Note: Main processor. Runs the pitch-detection DSP on one core and the display on the other, with PSRAM for the audio buffer and both I2S peripherals so the mic and amp run at once.
Captures the instrument for scale detection and tuning, with a digital output that avoids any analog front-end.
Shows the tonic, scale and sargam. The round format suits the tuner dial, taal cycle and circle-of-fifths views.
Combines the DAC and amplifier in one part so the processor drives the drone and metronome click directly.
Sets the tempo, pitch and mode, coupled to the knurled bezel so the whole ring turns and can be adjusted by feel.
Reproduces the drone and click, sized to fit the 70mm enclosure.
Pulses the beat so the player feels time instead of hearing it, making the metronome usable in an ensemble or under headphones.
Charges the cell over USB-C with over-charge, over-discharge and short-circuit protection.
Gives about 8 hours of untethered use so the device works on a music stand rather than beside an outlet.
Validate the full circuit and firmware before committing to a PCB, so design errors are caught while they cost nothing.
